title: Stoker metadata — game
description: `games/<slug>/game.yaml`: what a title is and every store's ids for it, its DLC and editions, the facts that hold for all of its copies — where it saves, what its store page says — and the fixes that hold across its releases. Everything here is what Stoker needs to make the game work and cannot read from its files; the presentation is kept as a convenience.

id.description: The title's own id, minted once and never changed: the anchor every store's ids map onto. Not a store's id — a GOG-only title has no AppId, and an anchor built from one store's id makes every other store second-class — and not a title, which gets renamed.

slug.description: The folder's name: readable, unique in the repository. A rename may move the folder; the id stays.

kind.description: `tool` is something that is not itself playable: a config tool, a level editor, a mod manager. Shared runtimes (Visual C++, DirectX) are not games and live in the runtime catalogue.

name.description: The title as its publisher writes it, trademark signs removed.

sortName.description: What to sort by when it differs from the name: `Witcher 3, The`.

stores.description: Every store's ids for the base game (`common.schema.json#/$defs/storeIds`). Reported by every install of it.

tags.description: The genres and features the stores list. A reader's own tags ("kids", "LAN night") are its own and are never here.

dlc.description: The game's DLC. A DLC is not a game: it has no releases, nothing to start and no achievements of its own (the stores keep those in its game's list). How a DLC gets into a copy, and whether an install has it, is not recorded: that depends on where the copy came from (Steam's depots, Epic's install tags, GOG's installers), and is the reader's own knowledge.

editions.description: The editions the game is sold as besides itself — a special edition is usually the base game plus a few DLC. An edition holds no content of its own and is never installed as such; what it is, is what it includes.

fixes.description: Patches and mods for the game's copies — applied last, after a build's own fixes and its release's — to whichever copies their `when` holds for. Written against a file's bytes, a fix here reaches every copy that has them, from any store or from disk, including one that matches no build this repository describes.

plugins.description: Plugins for the game's copies, in load order, each narrowed by its `when` (`common.schema.json#/$defs/pluginAssignment`).

hooks.description: Export hooks for the game's copies, each narrowed by its `when` (`common.schema.json#/$defs/hook`).

notes.description: What somebody getting this game to run needs to know and nothing else records: a quirk, a dead end, why a setting is what it is. Markdown.

overlayMode.description: How Stoker's in-game overlay is presented: `inFrame` draws into the game's own frames, `window` stacks windows over it, `off` shows nothing — for a game whose frames it cannot draw into, or that misbehaves with any overlay.

storePage.description: The facts a store page gives. Its words and pictures are archived (`presentation`).

sources.description: The stores the page was read from, in the order their values were merged.

slug.description: The tag's identity: what two stores' spellings converge on ("Co-op", "co op" → `co-op`).

kind.description: `genre` is what sort of game it is; `feature` what it supports.

links.description: Where else it is documented — PCGamingWiki, a store page, a fix's home. For a person reading the entry; nothing follows them.

dlc.description: One piece of downloadable content: an expansion, a soundtrack, a cosmetic pack.

id.description: Minted once, like a game's id: what requirements and editions refer to it by, and what a reader keys its own record of an install's DLC by.

name.description: The name it is sold under, trademark signs removed. The full name ("Example — Soundtrack"), not a bare "Soundtrack" that only makes sense beside its game.

requires.description: Other DLC of the same game this one needs installed beside it — directly; what it needs through them is walked, never listed.

includes.description: For a DLC that is a bundle of other DLC of the same game — a season pass, a collection: owning it means owning those. Its own reported ids are reported by an install that carries every DLC it includes, as an edition's are.

stores.description: Its own ids. Reported by an install that carries it.

notes.description: That its content ships inside the base game's files, that it only works from a certain release on. Markdown.

edition.description: A way the game is sold: the base game plus the DLC in `includes`. Importing or matching by an edition's store id means the base game and everything it includes; an install reports an edition's ids when it carries every DLC the edition includes. Content only one edition gets is a DLC it includes, not a special case.

includes.description: The DLC of this game it comes with. Empty for an edition that is the base game under another product (a Steam edition sold as its own package).

saves.description: Where the game keeps what a player would lose with the machine: saves and settings outside any store's cloud API, which Stoker syncs around every run for each player.

path.description: A glob with forward slashes that matches files, starting at a placeholder (the README's table): `*` and `?` match within one folder name, `**` matches any number of folders, none included — so `<winAppData>/Game/*.sav` is the folder's own `.sav` files and `<winAppData>/Game/**/*` everything in it and every folder below. Matched case-insensitively. A path naming a folder matches nothing. A Windows build that runs under Wine or Proton reads its Windows entries, with the `<win…>` placeholders inside its prefix (`drive_c/users/<user>/AppData/…`); a `<win…>` placeholder on any other system names no folder.

origin.description: `steam` when the entry is Steam Auto-Cloud's rule as published, `curated` when a contributor wrote or corrected it. An import from a store replaces that store's entries and never a curated one.

enabled.description: False to overrule a store's entry and keep it overruled: the entry stays, so a re-import does not bring it back.

key.description: The key with its hive spelt out and forward slashes: `HKEY_CURRENT_USER/Software/Example/Hexagon`. Everything below it counts.

savePlatforms.description: The systems the entry is for — the system the build is for, not the machine it runs on: a Windows build under Wine or Proton on Linux reads its `windows` entries, with the `<win…>` placeholders inside its prefix. Absent: every system. Never a store: an entry is about where the game writes, which the files decide.
